tradesNote: What a trade's pictures show and must not show, matched against each photograph's alt. The trade the brief names first applies; the other trades it names are its own too (a bakery and cafe shows its coffee), and so are the dishes of a restaurant or of a brief with a kitchen (dishes): their things are never banned. The deal leaves out a neighbouring trade's things (off), a landmark the brief does not name, a photograph that shows a logo, a house number, a plate or the inside of a café (unusable: another café's room passes for the client's), and the trade's stock shot. It deals at most half of the trade's things, then at most half of its places (two at most), the ones least dealt lately leading and the ones the trade's last deal listed behind the others, so two deals of one brief share no photograph while the library holds others; a place leads only where none of its things is left. A portfolio is dealt none of the things (its work is its own) and one of its place at most. Where a trade lists places ([brief pattern, place pattern]), the first the brief names is its place (a guesthouse on a fjord is shown by the sea, never a whitewashed village). A brief with no listed trade is matched by its own words. A set marked matchOnly (each photograph one trade's hands or one object) gives only the photographs that name the brief's own things; the people set (marked people) never stands for a listed trade's things or place, since a person there would pass for a guest or a customer. A trade may list its product: on a product page with no photographs of its own, a photograph whose alt names it, or the brief's own word for the product, is never dealt (another maker's product passes for the client's, however cropped), so there the pictures are its use, its load and its place, and a place may lead. A trade may list its first searches of the open collections (queries, with its place searched with placeWord), which never name the client's own thing; on a product page one that names its product is left out. A trade lists the sets its photographs are dealt from (sets), by fit: a cafe never from the night streets or a bar, a place to stay never from offices, a bike never from cars. A day trade (day: a cafe, a bakery, a bike) is dealt no photograph of night, nightlife or neon (night). A trade marked town (a cafe, a bakery, a brewery, a place to stay) is dealt no library place where the brief names its town and none of its listed places: another city's street or coast would pass for its own, so the sheet sends the builder to search it. A trade with fewer than six of its things in the library (counted before the direction's tone) tells the builder to search the open collections first with its queries, the dealt ones only the fallback. A place to stay whose name names a light, or whose brief names a northern place (north), is dealt no warm coast (warm: turquoise water, white sand, palms, chalk or limestone cliffs): a sunnier coast would stand in for its own.

trades.name: coffee
trades.show: the coffee in the cup and the beans close, a cup by a window, the street at its door; its own bar, counter and roaster only in its own pictures
trades.not: wine, beer, cocktails or tea; a restaurant's plated food; a bakery's bread

trades.name: bread
trades.show: the bread close (the crust, the crumb, dough rising in a bowl), the street at its door; its own counter and oven only in its own pictures
trades.not: coffee as the subject; a restaurant's plated food; wine or beer

trades.name: wine
trades.show: where it grows: the vines, the grapes at harvest, the hills in their light; its own bottle, cellar and glass only in its own pictures
trades.not: beer, coffee or spirits; a cocktail bar

trades.name: beer
trades.show: what it is made of: hops, malt and barley close, the field, the street at its door; its own brewhouse, tanks and glass only in its own pictures

trades.name: room details
trades.show: where the house stands (the shore, the mountain or the village), and for its rooms the details that belong to no one: bed linen in window light, a chair by the window, a cup on the bedside table, the view from a window
trades.not: a city skyline; a pool at sunset; an office; a whole room, a hotel or another house shown as this one

trades.name: bike
trades.show: the ride and the load without another maker's bike: the shopping in a crate, a child's helmet on a hook, the school run on foot, the city street in the rain
trades.not: cars, vans, motorbikes or scooters; a road or racing bike; a trike when the bike has two wheels; another maker's bike, its name or its logo

trades.name: furniture
trades.show: the materials close (oak grain, linen, steel) and light on a plain wall or floor; its own pieces, rooms and workshop only in its own pictures
trades.not: another maker's showroom; food on a table as the subject
queries: morning light on a white wall

trades.name: films
trades.show: frames and stills of its own films, large
trades.not: a mixing desk or a microphone (that is sound); a camera on a tripod; a typewriter

trades.name: ceramics
trades.show: the materials close (raw clay, a glaze colour as a surface) and light on a plain table or wall; its own pieces, wheel and kiln only in its own pictures
trades.not: food on plates as the subject; another trade's hands
queries: morning light on a white wall
